chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not go to the chicks in their nests, nor to the birds while they are sleeping, until morning comes. And do not go to the chick in its nest until it has grown feathers. When it flies, then draw your bow for it and set your snare for it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'These two narrations, although their apparent meaning indicates prohibition, we have directed them to a type of dislike (karahah) because it was narrated that there is 'no harm in night hunting.' We reconciled them with this interpretation so that the narrations do not contradict each other, and among what was narrated regarding the permissibility of that is what he narrated:'

key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislike (a legal status between permissibility and prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between prohibition and dislike in hunting birds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to illustrate the principle of *jam'* (reconciliation) between seemingly contradictory hadiths regarding bird hunting. He explains that while the text appears to prohibit taking chicks or sleeping birds, it is interpreted as *karahat* (dislike) rather than absolute prohibition (*haram*) to harmonize with other reports permitting night hunting. This scholarly resolution highlights the nuanced approach of Shia jurists in deriving practical legal rulings from textual evidence.
